subject: Tethered connectivity: allowlist and outbound guardrails for private endpoints
messages:

Subject: Private endpoints — initial IP ranges and high level ask

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the call earlier. As discussed, ACME is preparing to onboard Redwood Private within a locked VPC; procurement and security are aligned but networking needs a clear outbound policy to satisfy our audit team. Attaching the current egress CIDR blocks we control.

Quick asks to start:
- Can Redwood confirm the minimal set of destination IPs/FQDNs we need to allow for control plane + runtime?
- Any TLS SNI or header requirements to avoid deep inspection?
- Do you have a recommended firewall rule precedence and an evidence package we can attach to our SOC team?

Attached: safelist-ip-matrix.csv (internal ranges we control).

Appreciate a short checklist we can share with network ops.

—Beth
Beth Anys
Dir, Infrastructure Engineering | ACME Corporation
beth.anys@acme.com | +1 415-555-0183
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private endpoints — initial IP ranges and high level ask

Hi Beth — thanks for sending the CIDRs. Looping in Marissa (Security/compliance lead) and Jordan (Network eng) to propose a concise allowlist and outbound guardrail set.

High level answers up front:
- Minimal destinations: control plane (region-specific), model artifact storage (S3-style endpoints or our object store), telemetry/metrics endpoints, and optional registry updates. We will provide an exact FQDN + fallback IP set per region.
- TLS/SNI: Redwood supports SNI-based routing; we recommend allowing SNI match to inbound hostnames we provide to reduce FQDN allowlist size. No custom header requirements; mTLS for Private controlplane can be enabled per contract.
- Evidence package: Marissa will attach a compact PDF with recommended rule wording, justification, and audit checklist.

Action items from our side:
1) We will produce a one-page firewall policy (rules + priority) and an evidence bundle (fw-policy-digest.pdf).
2) A definitive allowlist CSV with primary FQDNs and fallback IPs mapped to the CIDRs you provided (to be delivered by Mon).
3) A short runbook for temporary exceptions / canary testing window (30-min backout).

Can you confirm the target cutover date window for connectivity? That will affect the ephemeral IP rotation guidance.

Thanks,
Sofia Ivanova
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Beth Anys <beth.anys@acme.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private endpoints — initial IP ranges and high level ask

Thanks — attaching the policy draft (fw-policy-digest.pdf). Below are the recommended firewall rules and rationale; please treat as minimal controls for the Private runtime and control plane.

Recommended rule set (apply in this priority order):
1) Allow TCP 443 to controlplane-<region>.redwood.ai (SNI: controlplane.redwood.ai) — management, rollouts, health checks.
2) Allow TCP 443 to artifacts.redwood.ai and region-specific storage endpoints (SNI matches: artifacts.redwood.ai OR s3.<region>.amazonaws.com).
3) Allow UDP/53 to your DNS resolvers only; block outbound DNS to arbitrary IPs to prevent exfiltration.
4) Allow TCP 443 to telemetry-redwood.redwood.ai (optional: destination port pinned).
5) Deny all other outbound ports/addresses by default (explicit deny) with logging to your SIEM.

Notes and finer points:
- Use SNI allowlist where possible. If your firewall can't do SNI matching, use the small set of IPs in the CSV we will send as a fallback.
- Ephemeral egress IPs: If you require stable source IPs for Redwood-to-ACME callbacks, we can provide a small set of NAT egress IPs for your inbound ACLs — this requires reserved capacity in the contract (we noted that on the call).
- Evidence: fw-policy-digest.pdf includes rule text, the expected hit-rate profile, required logs (TLS SNI, dest IP, timestamp), and suggested retention window for audit (90 days).

Attachment: fw-policy-digest.pdf (policy + example firewall snippets).

Jordan — can you confirm the SNI hostnames and the two fallback IP blocks (us-west-2) so Sofia can include them in the CSV?

—Marissa

Beth — attaching the final CSV and the evidence bundle links. Below is the condensed checklist you can hand to network ops during change window.

Attached items (sent):
- safelist-ip-matrix.csv — columns: service, primary_fqdn, sni_string, fallback_ips, purpose, notes
- fw-policy-digest.pdf — firewall snippets, audit guidance, and sample JSON log schema

Short change window checklist for pilot (non-prod):
1) Apply allow rules (1–4 from Marissa) in staging firewall with SNI matches first.
2) If firewall lacks SNI, add fallback IPs for each service per CSV.
3) Restrict DNS to internal resolvers and configure DNS forwarders for external lookups.
4) Turn on TLS SNI logging (sample JSON logs in fw-policy-digest.pdf).
5) Open a 60-minute canary window: exercise health checks, artifact pulls, and telemetry ingestion. Monitor logs for any DENY events.
6) If DENY count > 0 for essential services in the first 10 minutes, rollback via rule remove and collect logs for triage.

Notes: recommended DNS TTL for artifacts is 300s to 900s depending on your caching layer. We include a JSON log example in fw-policy-digest.pdf that shows fields your SOC requested: timestamp, src_ip, dst_ip, dst_sni, dst_fqdn, action, bytes, request_id.

Next steps:
- Sofia will upload the CSV + policy to the Confluence runbook (link included).
- Marissa will generate the short audit cover letter for procurement to attach to the contract.
- Jordan will hold the reserved egress IP pool request ticket until we have firm dates.

DocuSign link for the outbound-ip reservation addendum (if you choose reserved egress): https://app.docusign.com/ACME/Envelope/Env-99221

I'll follow up with the Confluence link and HubSpot note once uploaded.

Thanks — Sofia
